$comment: A CAMPUS-TREND NOTIFICATION FOR A POST THIS DEVICE ALREADY DISPLAYED SHOWS NOTHING, WRITTEN ONCE AND ASSERTED ON EVERY PLATFORM.
Owner, 2026-11-24 ('Verif sur l'appareil'): a 'Suggestion : ...' notification can announce a post the member already
saw in the feed, because the server records no 'seen' (principles 1 and 3 of docs/principes.md). The DEVICE keeps a
local record of the posts it displayed; a trend for one of them shows no banner and no bell row. NOTHING is sent to
the server. The accepted limit: a post seen on another device is not recognised.
The device's copy is `seen_posts.json` (written by Rust `store_seen_posts` from what the WebView holds,
`seenPosts.svelte.ts`): `userId` is its owner; `posts` maps a post id (lower-case uuid) to the epoch milliseconds of
its `publishedAt`, which is what the writer prunes by (a post older than `trendWindowHours` plus a grace can never be
announced as a trend again - the server's `TREND_WINDOW_HOURS`, asserted equal by `campus-trend-window.contract.spec.ts`).
A push is a trend when its `contentKey` is one of `trendKeys` - the FIELD, never the wording - and it names its post in
`postId`. Readers: the client's `isSeenTrend` (seenPosts.ts, against the same shape), Android `SeenTrends` (the FCM
service), the iOS extension, `canari_push.mm` and Rust's writer, on these cases. A reader applies no age rule: an
entry that outlived its window names a post no trend can name again.
Case fields: `me` the signed-in account (`push_context.json`); `contentKey` and `postId` the push's own fields;
`expected` true when the push is withheld on this device, false when it is shown as before.
